summary: New experimental component text-swap — the second of ADR 0028's owned motion components, built on Presence. A short label replaced in place: the old words fade out on --ui-duration-fast without moving, the new ones arrive on --ui-duration-base with Presence's rise, and the box holding them eases between the two measured widths, so a button never snaps narrower under the pointer that pressed it. Layers share one grid cell, left-aligned and clipped sideways only; the leaving copy is inert and aria-hidden, so a host's accessible name follows the new words at once; a word that comes back mid-swap turns around and a rapid sequence retargets from the current width. At Reduced the rise goes and the cross-fade and width stay; at Off everything is 1ms. Designed and built overnight without review: the sheet (Components - Drafts) badges its own readings — width on base, left-aligned clipped layers, an unclipped vertical axis — as Derived for the maintainer. check:utilities' shared class extractor now blanks data-* attribute values, which it read as classes once a slot name began with a utility prefix (text-swap → --color-swap); a real bad class beside it is still caught (probed). The presence alias is now in every resolver, since TextSwap is the first item to import it.
